story.text: Hi, welcome to Alice Wonderlab. It’s so lovely to meet you. ♡
I thought I’d start with the story behind the name.

When I was little, the grown-ups around me always said I had a knack for making things. My head was full of new ideas, and I loved getting hands-on, bringing those wild little imaginings to life, one step at a time.
So they gave me the English name Alice, inspired by Alice in Wonderland.
As I’ve grown up, that love of creating and exploring has stayed with me.
These days, with so much moving so quickly, we’ve grown used to getting to know someone through a photo, a few lines in a bio, or a video that lasts just a few seconds.
But can a few seconds really tell someone’s whole story?
This time, I wanted to try something a little different.
To turn a traditional portfolio into a little world you can step into and explore for yourself.
We may not have met before, but I hope this gives you a warmer, more playful way to take your time and get to know the real me.
That’s how Alice Wonderlab began.

I called it a Lab because I wanted it to be more than a place to share stories and show my work. I wanted a little space where I could keep exploring, try out new ideas, and actually bring them to life.
This little milk tea shop is my very first experiment.
To be honest, with my background in communication, 3D modeling was completely new to me.

From learning the software and designing the scene to finding a home for each little cat, lamp, and quiet corner, I spent many nights figuring things out from scratch. I tried things, changed them, and tried again, slowly building the little shop I’d imagined.
I hope you have fun here. And I hope this slightly different way of meeting helps you get to know the real Alice a little better.
Well, that’s enough storytelling from me for now.
Why not wander over to another corner of the shop?
You might meet a few sweet cats, hear a song that’s kept me company for years, or stumble upon a little secret tucked away somewhere.
The rest of the story is yours to discover.
